comments.text:
I have many years of competitive go-kart racing, both in sprint and endurance formats. I've had good results, and some bad crashes (currently recovering from one). There is nothing I can tell you that your coach probably hasn't said already, but I'll say it anyways as a reminder to others who may read this: 1) Never drive angry. It's a sure way to end up in the wall. 2) Know your limits, and don't take leaps of faith. Work your way up and result will come. If you push too much too soon you'll end up in the wall. 3) You have nothing to prove. 4) A lot more people remember when you end up int the wall than when you end up in first place.
About that injury: someone spun me around and another guy drove straight into me at full speed. I was projected from the kart. Tibial shaft spiral fracture & fibula head fracture, plus shattered and sunk tibial plate, broken ribs, and broken hand fingers. Not a fun one. I'm probably done with go-kart racing. I hope you don't experience this part of racing.
